native.method: Native headed Chrome UI Ctrl+0 and Ctrl+= via X11 XTest on Xvfb. Native zoom independently checked from devicePixelRatio and unchanged outer window with inverse inner width/height. No CSS zoom, pinch scale or CDP device emulation in native tests. Targeted font/line-height doubling and text-spacing overrides are labelled separately.
native.screenshots: Actual X11 Chrome window pixels, including browser chrome, not the invalid earlier CDP native captures. Blank content and visible-heading captures fail.

diagnostics.finding: Missing runner xwininfo. Failed before browser checks; replaced dependency with direct X11 access.
Legacy window title/root-only lookup failed before observations. Corrected UTF-8 name and window-tree lookup.
Original native metrics and individual spacing passed; combined doubled text plus spacing clipped at 320/360px. The green diagnostic job retained these as stress findings, not quality passes.

Repair passed 66 conditions and ordinary parity, but inspection found blank CDP captures at native 200%. These images are invalid visual evidence; later real-window captures supersede them without discarding valid recorded DOM metrics.

One enlarged heading screenshot differed because of the intended word wrapping. All geometry comparisons passed. Exact state/text/typography/glyph-fit checks now bound that one text region; all remaining image pixels and all ordinary comparisons keep existing gates.

One 1440px Books menu raster differed by 0.06352632179970309 despite unchanged measured bounds. Original fractional origins differed by 0.0625px; both captures were aligned to x431. Inspection showed a text raster displacement. A single unchanged diagnostic replay followed localisation, without runtime, assertion or threshold changes. Passing replay does not establish a permanent fix or causal certainty.

manualInspection.scope: Representative originals inspected for actual heading text, borders, native zoom, short-screen controls and normal appearance. Not every screenshot was independently visually reviewed.
